questions.explanation: The three-year retention requirement covers listings, agency disclosure forms, closing statements, and related documents, and the records must be produced on the Department's request.

questions.prompt: A broker's obligation to supervise the activities of associated salespersons means the broker:
choices: May be disciplined for a salesperson's violations the broker failed to supervise against
Is liable only for violations the broker personally directed
Must review every advertisement after it has been published
Must accompany salespersons to all closings
questions.explanation: Supervision is an affirmative duty. A broker who does not exercise it can face discipline for conduct they never knew about.

questions.prompt: A salesperson who is not paid an agreed commission by their broker may:
choices: Sue the broker, but has no claim against the seller
Sue the seller directly for the unpaid amount
File a lien against the property that was sold
Collect the amount directly from the buyer at closing
questions.explanation: The salesperson's contractual relationship is with the sponsoring broker alone. Only a licensed broker may bring an action for a commission against a principal.

questions.prompt: An unlicensed assistant working for a brokerage may lawfully:
choices: Schedule appointments and place advertisements the broker has approved
Answer a caller's questions about a listing's condition and terms
Host an open house and collect visitor information
Explain the agency disclosure form to a prospective buyer
questions.explanation: Unlicensed staff may perform clerical and administrative work. Anything requiring judgment about a property, or that solicits or negotiates, requires a license.

questions.prompt: Two competing brokerages agree to charge sellers the same commission rate. This is:
choices: Price fixing, a per se violation of federal antitrust law
Lawful, provided the rate is disclosed to sellers in writing
Lawful, because commission rates are set by local custom
A violation only if the brokerages together hold a majority of listings
questions.explanation: Commission rates are always negotiable between a broker and their own client. Agreements among competitors to set them are illegal without regard to market share or intent.
questions.citation: Sherman Antitrust Act; DOS 77-hour curriculum § Law of Agency

questions.prompt: Two brokerages agree that one will work only the north side of town and the other only the south. This is:
choices: Market allocation, which is prohibited under antitrust law
A permissible efficiency arrangement if disclosed to clients
Lawful, because brokers may choose where to do business
A group boycott, actionable only by the excluded competitor
questions.explanation: Allocating territories or customer types among competitors restrains trade. A broker may unilaterally decide where to work; agreeing with a competitor to divide the market is the violation.
questions.citation: Sherman Antitrust Act; DOS 77-hour curriculum § Law of Agency

questions.prompt: A licensee knows the basement floods every spring but says nothing, and the buyer cannot see any evidence during a walkthrough. This is:
choices: Failure to disclose a known latent defect
Permissible, because the buyer had the right to order an inspection
Puffing, since flooding severity is a matter of opinion
Permissible, because the duty runs only to the licensee's own client
questions.explanation: Latent defects are those not discoverable by reasonable inspection. Known material defects must be disclosed to buyers even when the buyer is a customer rather than a client.

questions.prompt: Under New York law, a seller or licensee has no liability for failing to disclose that a homicide occurred in the house because:
choices: Real Property Law §443-a provides that no cause of action arises from that non-disclosure
The federal Fair Housing Act preempts any such disclosure requirement
Such events are considered latent defects that only an inspector may report
The buyer is presumed to have researched the property's history
questions.explanation: New York addresses stigmatized property by statute. The protection also covers a death on the property and prior occupancy by a person with HIV or AIDS.

questions.prompt: A buyer asks a licensee whether any registered sex offenders live nearby. The licensee should:
choices: Direct the buyer to the state's public sex offender registry
Research the registry and report the findings to the buyer
Decline to respond, because the question implicates fair housing law
Ask the seller to disclose the information in writing
questions.explanation: Referring the buyer to the public registry lets them get current information directly, and avoids the licensee becoming responsible for the accuracy of what they report.

questions.prompt: A licensee receives a second offer while a first offer is pending seller review. The licensee must:
choices: Present the second offer to the seller promptly
Hold the second offer until the seller responds to the first
Present it only if it exceeds the first offer
Return it to the submitting agent as untimely
questions.explanation: All offers must be presented promptly until closing unless the seller has instructed otherwise in writing. Screening offers substitutes the licensee's judgment for the client's.

questions.prompt: The distinction between a client and a customer is that a client:
choices: Is owed full fiduciary duties, while a customer is owed honesty and fair dealing
Has signed a purchase contract, while a customer has not
Pays the commission, while a customer does not
Is represented by a broker, while a customer is represented by an attorney
questions.explanation: The client is the principal in the agency relationship. Customers are third parties the licensee deals with honestly but does not represent.

questions.prompt: An agent whose authority is limited to a single transaction, such as selling one listed property, holds:
choices: A special agency
A general agency
A universal agency
An agency coupled with an interest
questions.explanation: A listing agreement creates a special agency. Property management, involving a continuing series of acts, creates a general agency.

questions.prompt: A principal who accepts the benefit of an unauthorized act performed by their agent has effectively:
choices: Ratified the act, giving it the same effect as if it had been authorized
Terminated the agency by operation of law
Created an agency coupled with an interest
Waived all fiduciary duties for the remainder of the transaction
questions.explanation: Ratification is retroactive approval. It is one of the ways an agency relationship, or an individual act within one, can be created after the fact.

questions.prompt: A licensee associated with one broker wishes to move to another brokerage. The licensee must:
choices: Have the change of association filed with the Department of State before working for the new broker
Wait ninety days from the date of termination before affiliating
Surrender the license and apply for a new one
Obtain written consent from the prior broker's clients
questions.explanation: A license is only active while associated with a sponsoring broker. The termination and the new association must both be recorded with the Department.
questions.citation: RPL §441-b; DOS 77-hour curriculum § License Law and Regulations

questions.prompt: An associate broker is best described as a person who:
choices: Holds a broker's license but works under the supervision of another broker
Holds a salesperson's license and supervises other salespersons
Is licensed only to manage property, not to sell it
Has passed the broker exam but has not yet been licensed
questions.explanation: An associate broker has met the full broker qualifications but chooses to operate under a supervising broker rather than run their own office.
questions.citation: RPL §440(2); DOS 77-hour curriculum § License Law and Regulations

questions.prompt: The consequence of undisclosed dual agency in New York can include:
choices: Loss of the commission and disciplinary action against the license
A fine payable to the buyer, but no effect on the license
Automatic voiding of the deed after closing
Nothing, provided both parties were treated fairly
questions.explanation: Courts have denied commissions to brokers who represented both sides without informed consent, and the Department of State treats it as grounds for suspension or revocation.

questions.prompt: An exclusive listing agreement in New York should contain:
choices: A definite termination date rather than an automatic renewal provision
A commission rate set by the local board of realtors
A clause waiving the seller's right to reject offers
The names of every cooperating broker who may show the property
questions.explanation: Open-ended listings and automatic renewals trap sellers in agreements they may not realize are still running. A definite end date is the expected practice.

questions.prompt: A multiple listing service is best described as:
choices: A cooperative arrangement among brokers to share listings and offers of compensation
A government registry of all properties for sale in a county
A licensing category regulated by the Department of State
An agency relationship between the seller and every member broker
questions.explanation: The MLS is a private cooperative among member brokers. Membership does not itself create an agency relationship between a member and another member's client.

questions.prompt: An agency coupled with an interest differs from an ordinary agency because it:
choices: Cannot be revoked unilaterally by the principal, since the agent holds a stake in the property
Terminates automatically upon the death of the agent
Requires no written agreement of any kind
May be created only between family members
questions.explanation: Where the agent has an actual financial interest in the subject property, revocation would destroy that interest, so the usual right of the principal to revoke at will does not apply.

questions.prompt: A seller who will be out of the country grants another person written authority to sign closing documents. That instrument is:
choices: A power of attorney, and the person acting under it is an attorney-in-fact
A listing agreement with an assignment clause
An agency disclosure form with a substitution rider
A proprietary lease naming a successor
questions.explanation: An attorney-in-fact need not be a lawyer. For a conveyance, the power of attorney must generally be acknowledged and recorded along with the deed.

questions.prompt: A licensee states that a property is connected to municipal sewer when it is actually on a septic system. The licensee believed the statement was true. This is:
choices: A negligent misrepresentation, actionable even without intent to deceive
Puffing, because utility connections vary by neighborhood
Fraud, because the statement was objectively false
Not actionable, because the buyer could have verified it
questions.explanation: Intent separates fraud from negligent misrepresentation, but both can create liability. A licensee is expected to verify material facts rather than repeat assumptions.

questions.prompt: Errors and omissions insurance for a real estate licensee covers:
choices: Claims arising from negligent acts in the course of professional services
Intentional fraud committed by the licensee
Fines imposed by the Department of State
Physical damage occurring at a property during a showing
questions.explanation: E and O policies respond to professional negligence. Deliberate wrongdoing is excluded, which is a common source of surprise for licensees who assume the policy covers everything.

questions.prompt: An exclusive right to represent buyer agreement obligates the buyer to:
choices: Work through that broker for the purchase of any property during the term
Purchase a property within the stated term or forfeit a deposit
Pay the broker directly regardless of what the seller offers
Disclose the agreement to every listing agent before viewing a property
questions.explanation: The agreement makes the broker the buyer's exclusive representative for the term. Compensation may still come from the listing side, from the buyer, or from a combination.

questions.prompt: The source of a buyer's agent's compensation:
choices: Does not by itself determine whom the agent represents
Always determines whom the agent represents
Must always be the buyer, to avoid dual agency
Must always be the listing broker, under New York law
questions.explanation: Representation follows the agency agreement, not the money. A buyer's agent paid out of the listing side still owes fiduciary duties to the buyer.

questions.prompt: A licensee refers a client to a mortgage lender and receives a fee for the referral. In a federally related residential loan, this is:
choices: Prohibited as an unearned kickback
Permitted if the client is told the amount at closing
Permitted if the fee is under $500
Permitted if the lender discloses it on the closing statement
questions.explanation: RESPA bars fees for the mere referral of settlement service business. Payment must be for services actually performed, and disclosure does not cure an otherwise unearned fee.

questions.prompt: A sales team operating within a brokerage advertises under its own name. The advertisement must also:
choices: Include the name of the brokerage the team operates under
State the team's total sales volume for the prior year
Identify each licensed member of the team
Be filed with the Department of State before publication
questions.explanation: A team is not a separate licensed entity. Advertising must make clear which licensed brokerage stands behind it so consumers know who they are actually dealing with.

questions.prompt: An apartment information vendor in New York is a person who:
choices: Sells prospective tenants lists of available apartments for a fee
Manages residential rental buildings on behalf of owners
Negotiates commercial leases for corporate tenants
Inspects apartments for code compliance before occupancy
questions.explanation: This is a distinct New York licensed category with its own contract and refund requirements, created because selling apartment lists invited abuse.
questions.citation: RPL Article 12-A; DOS 77-hour curriculum § License Law and Regulations

questions.prompt: A licensee's duty of confidentiality regarding a former client's financial situation:
choices: Continues indefinitely after the transaction closes
Ends when the transaction closes
Ends one year after the agency terminates
Ends when the client engages a different brokerage
questions.explanation: Confidentiality is the duty that outlives the relationship. A licensee who later represents a different party must not use or reveal what a former client told them in confidence.

questions.prompt: A licensee lists a property, then arranges for a relative to buy it below market without telling the seller of the relationship. This is:
choices: Self-dealing, a breach of the duty of loyalty
Permissible, since the seller accepted the price
A permissible transaction requiring only post-closing disclosure
Dual agency, curable by written consent after closing
questions.explanation: Loyalty requires the agent to put the client's interests ahead of their own and those of people close to them. The relationship must be disclosed before the seller decides.
questions.citation: 19 NYCRR §175.7; DOS 77-hour curriculum § Law of Agency

questions.prompt: In a designated sales agent arrangement, the broker who makes the designations:
choices: Remains a dual agent and may not advocate for either party
Becomes the seller's agent only
Withdraws from the transaction entirely
May advise both designated agents on negotiating strategy
questions.explanation: Designation splits advocacy between two individual licensees, but the brokerage itself is still on both sides. The designating broker stays neutral.

questions.prompt: A tie-in arrangement, in which a builder sells a lot on the condition that the buyer use the builder's construction company, is:
choices: An antitrust concern because it conditions one product on the purchase of another
Permissible whenever both prices are disclosed
Permissible because the builder owns both businesses
A form of dual agency requiring written consent
questions.explanation: Tying uses market power over one product to force the sale of a second. It is a recurring issue where sellers control both the land and a related service.

questions.prompt: A listing agreement may be terminated before its expiration date by:
choices: Mutual agreement of the seller and the broker
The broker's unilateral decision to stop advertising
The seller's oral statement to a cooperating agent
The expiration of the buyer's mortgage commitment
questions.explanation: Beyond mutual agreement, listings end by performance, expiration, or operation of law such as the death of a party or destruction of the property. Simply losing interest does not end the contract.

questions.prompt: A licensee prepares an opinion of value for a lender deciding whether to grant a mortgage. In that context the licensee:
choices: Should decline, because a lending decision generally requires a licensed or certified appraiser
May proceed, because a comparative market analysis is equivalent to an appraisal
May proceed if the opinion is labeled a broker price opinion
May proceed if the licensee has five years of experience
questions.explanation: A comparative market analysis or broker price opinion supports pricing and marketing decisions. Valuation for a lending decision falls under appraisal regulation.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Valuation Process and Pricing Properties

questions.prompt: The scope of an agent's authority matters because a principal is bound by:
choices: Acts within the authority the principal actually or apparently granted
Every act the agent performs while the agency is in effect
Only acts the principal approved in writing beforehand
Only acts the agent performed in the principal's presence
questions.explanation: Apparent authority is what makes this practical: if the principal's conduct leads a third party to reasonably believe the agent is authorized, the principal can be bound.

questions.prompt: A seller instructs the listing agent not to show the home to families with children. The agent should:
choices: Refuse the instruction and explain that following it would violate fair housing law
Follow the instruction, since obedience is a fiduciary duty
Follow the instruction but document it in the file
Withdraw from the listing without explanation
questions.explanation: Obedience extends only to lawful instructions. Familial status is protected, and an agent who complies shares liability with the seller.
questions.citation: 42 U.S.C. §3604; DOS 77-hour curriculum § Law of Agency

questions.prompt: A brokerage that represents only buyers and never takes listings is practicing:
choices: Single agency, which avoids in-house dual agency entirely
Dual agency, because it deals with sellers in every transaction
Subagency, because it works through listing brokers
Designated agency, because each buyer gets one licensee
questions.explanation: Single agency means representing only one side of the transaction as a matter of business model, which removes the in-house conflict before it can arise.

questions.prompt: A seller's agent receives a full-price offer and a slightly lower offer with far stronger financing. The agent should:
choices: Present both and advise the seller on the relative strengths of each
Present only the full-price offer, since it meets the listing terms
Recommend the full-price offer without discussing the other
Ask both buyers to submit revised offers before presenting either
questions.explanation: Price is one term among several. The duties of disclosure and reasonable care require the agent to help the client evaluate financing strength, contingencies, and timing.

questions.prompt: The bundle of rights associated with real property ownership includes the rights of:
choices: Possession, use, enjoyment, exclusion, and disposition
Possession, taxation, escheat, and eminent domain
Use, occupancy, insurance, and financing
Disposition, zoning, assessment, and condemnation
questions.explanation: Taxation, escheat, eminent domain, and police power are the four government powers that limit ownership, not rights the owner holds.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Estates and Interests)

questions.prompt: Whether an item has become a fixture is determined chiefly by:
choices: The method of attachment, adaptation to the property, and the parties' intention
The original purchase price of the item
Whether the item can be removed without any tools
Whether the item was installed by a licensed contractor
questions.explanation: Intention is usually the controlling factor, with attachment and adaptation serving as evidence of it. Disputes are best avoided by naming the item in the contract.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Estates and Interests)

questions.prompt: A commercial tenant installs display shelving and a walk-in cooler for their business. At the end of the lease these are generally:
choices: Trade fixtures the tenant may remove, repairing any damage caused
Permanent fixtures that become the landlord's property
Personal property the landlord may sell to recover unpaid rent
Improvements the landlord must reimburse the tenant for
questions.explanation: Trade fixtures are an exception to the usual fixture rule. Items left behind after the lease ends generally become the landlord's by accession.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Estates and Interests)

questions.prompt: Growing crops planted by a tenant farmer, which the tenant may return to harvest after the tenancy ends, are:
choices: Emblements, treated as the tenant's personal property
Fixtures belonging to the landowner
Part of the real property conveyed with the land
Trade fixtures requiring removal before the lease expires
questions.explanation: The doctrine protects a tenant's investment of labor in annual crops. Naturally occurring vegetation, by contrast, passes with the land.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Estates and Interests)

questions.prompt: An owner whose land borders a large navigable lake holds:
choices: Littoral rights
Riparian rights
Prior appropriation rights
Percolating water rights
questions.explanation: Littoral rights attach to land bordering a lake, sea, or ocean. Riparian rights attach to land along a flowing watercourse such as a river or stream.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Estates and Interests)

questions.prompt: A neighbor's garage was built two feet over the boundary line onto the adjoining lot. This is:
choices: An encroachment, which a survey would reveal and which can cloud title
An easement by prescription, effective immediately upon construction
A license, revocable by the affected owner at any time
A party wall, jointly owned by both property owners
questions.explanation: Encroachments can make title unmarketable and, if left unchallenged long enough, ripen into a prescriptive easement or an adverse possession claim.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Liens and Easements)

questions.prompt: A landowner gives a neighbor spoken permission to cross the property to reach a fishing spot. This permission is:
choices: A license, revocable at will and not an interest in land
An easement appurtenant that runs with the land
An easement in gross benefiting the neighbor personally
An irrevocable easement by necessity
questions.explanation: A license is personal permission, not a property interest. Because it is revocable, it does not create the kind of continuous adverse use that would support a prescriptive claim.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Liens and Easements)

questions.prompt: A utility company's right to run power lines across many private parcels is:
choices: An easement in gross, which benefits an entity rather than an adjoining parcel
An easement appurtenant, benefiting each parcel it crosses
A license terminable when the property is sold
An encroachment subject to removal on demand
questions.explanation: There is no dominant tenement. Commercial easements in gross are assignable and survive the sale of the burdened land.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Liens and Easements)

questions.prompt: An owner subdivides a parcel, leaving one lot with no access to a public road. The landlocked owner is most likely entitled to:
choices: An easement by necessity
An easement by prescription after ten years
A license from the municipality
Compensation through inverse condemnation
questions.explanation: Easements by necessity arise when a conveyance leaves a parcel without access, on the reasoning that access was implicitly intended. No period of use is required.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Liens and Easements)

questions.prompt: The owner of the dominant tenement purchases the servient tenement. The easement between them:
choices: Terminates by merger, because one owner now holds both parcels
Continues, and revives automatically if the parcels are later separated
Converts into an easement in gross
Must be released by a recorded instrument to end
questions.explanation: An owner cannot hold an easement over their own land. If the parcels are later split, a new easement must be created; the old one does not spring back.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Liens and Easements)

questions.prompt: A wall standing on the boundary line and shared by two adjoining buildings is:
choices: A party wall, with each owner holding rights and maintenance obligations
An encroachment that the newer building's owner must remove
The sole property of whichever owner built it
Common area owned by the municipality
questions.explanation: Party wall arrangements are typically governed by a recorded agreement covering repair costs and the consequences of one building being demolished.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Liens and Easements)

questions.prompt: A notice of pendency, commonly called a lis pendens, is filed to:
choices: Warn prospective purchasers that litigation affecting title to the property is pending
Secure payment for labor and materials furnished to the property
Record the transfer of title from grantor to grantee
Establish the priority of a purchase money mortgage
questions.explanation: Anyone acquiring an interest after the notice is filed takes subject to the outcome of the lawsuit, which makes the property effectively unsaleable while it is in place.
questions.citation: CPLR Article 65; DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues

questions.prompt: A mortgage lien is best classified as:
choices: Voluntary and specific
Involuntary and specific
Voluntary and general
Involuntary and general
questions.explanation: The owner consents to it, which makes it voluntary, and it attaches to one identified property, which makes it specific. A judgment lien is the involuntary, general counterpart.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Liens and Easements)

questions.prompt: A legal description that traces boundaries using directions, distances, and monuments from a fixed starting point is:
choices: A metes and bounds description
A lot and block description
A rectangular survey description
A street address description
questions.explanation: Metes and bounds must return to the point of beginning to enclose the parcel. It is the older method and is common in the original thirteen states, including New York.

questions.prompt: A description reading "Lot 14, Block 3, of the Meadowbrook Subdivision as filed in the county clerk's office" is:
choices: A lot and block description, referring to a recorded subdivision plat
A metes and bounds description using recorded monuments
An informal description that is insufficient to convey title
A rectangular survey description based on principal meridians
questions.explanation: Also called the recorded plat method, this incorporates the filed map by reference, which is why the map itself must be recorded for the description to work.

questions.prompt: The clause in a deed that defines the extent of the ownership interest being conveyed, often beginning "to have and to hold," is the:
choices: Habendum clause
Granting clause
Defeasance clause
Acceleration clause
questions.explanation: The granting clause names the parties and states the intent to convey; the habendum clause that follows describes and limits the estate being granted.

questions.prompt: A deed must be acknowledged before a notary primarily so that it can be:
choices: Recorded in the public land records
Considered valid between the grantor and grantee
Used to transfer possession of the property
Accepted by the grantee's title insurer as a survey substitute
questions.explanation: Acknowledgment is a recording requirement, not a validity requirement. An unacknowledged deed can still pass title between the parties; it simply cannot go on the record.

questions.prompt: Recording a deed in the county clerk's office gives:
choices: Constructive notice to the world of the grantee's interest
Actual notice only to parties who search the records
A guarantee from the county that title is marketable
Priority over all previously recorded liens
questions.explanation: Constructive notice means everyone is charged with knowledge of what the record contains, whether or not they actually looked. Actual notice is what a person genuinely knows.

questions.prompt: Marketable title is best described as title that:
choices: A reasonable, well-informed buyer would accept without fear of litigation
Is guaranteed by the county recording office
Carries no mortgage or other voluntary lien
Has been held by the same family for at least ten years
questions.explanation: Marketable does not mean perfect. It means free of defects serious enough that a prudent buyer, properly advised, would refuse the property or face a lawsuit over it.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Title Closing and Costs)

questions.prompt: An old unreleased mortgage still appearing in the record, though the debt was long ago paid, is:
choices: A cloud on title, typically cleared by obtaining a satisfaction or a quitclaim deed
A latent defect that title insurance cannot cover
An encumbrance that automatically expires after ten years
A lien with priority over the current owner's mortgage
questions.explanation: Clouds are apparent defects that a title search turns up. A quiet title action is the remedy when the party who could release it cannot be found.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Title Closing and Costs)

questions.prompt: The chain of title is:
choices: The successive record of conveyances from the earliest owner to the present one
The list of liens currently encumbering the property
The sequence of mortgages recorded against the property
The insurer's schedule of exceptions to coverage
questions.explanation: A gap in the chain, where one conveyance is missing, is a defect that must be resolved before title can be insured or called marketable.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Title Closing and Costs)

questions.prompt: In a deed containing full covenants, the covenant of seisin is the grantor's promise that:
choices: The grantor owns the property and has the right to convey it
The grantee will not be disturbed in possession by a superior claim
The grantor will obtain any further documents needed to perfect title
The property is free of all encumbrances
questions.explanation: Quiet enjoyment covers undisturbed possession, further assurance covers additional documents, and against encumbrances covers liens. Seisin is the promise of ownership itself.

questions.prompt: A deed executed by a court-appointed official to convey property sold in a foreclosure is:
choices: A referee's deed, which carries no warranties of title
A full covenant and warranty deed
A bargain and sale deed with covenant against grantor's acts
A quitclaim deed executed by the former owner
questions.explanation: Officials conveying property they never personally owned give no warranties. Executor's deeds in estate sales work the same way.

questions.prompt: A person dies owning real property in New York with no will and no locatable heirs. The property:
choices: Escheats to the state
Passes to the county in which it is located as a tax lien
Is sold at public auction with proceeds to the school district
Vests in the adjoining property owners in equal shares
questions.explanation: Escheat is one of the four government powers over property. It prevents land from being left permanently ownerless.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Estates and Interests)

questions.prompt: A person who dies leaving a valid will is said to have died:
choices: Testate, with property passing to the devisees named in the will
Intestate, with property passing under the statute of descent
In escheat, with property passing to the state
Seised, with property passing to the surviving joint tenants
questions.explanation: Dying testate means the will controls, subject to probate. Dying intestate means the statute decides who inherits.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Estates and Interests)

questions.prompt: Two people hold title as joint tenants with right of survivorship. One conveys their interest to a third party. The result is that:
choices: The joint tenancy is severed and the new owner holds as a tenant in common
The conveyance is void, because joint tenants cannot convey separately
The remaining joint tenant automatically acquires the whole property
The new owner becomes a joint tenant with the remaining original owner
questions.explanation: A conveyance breaks the unities that joint tenancy requires. The buyer cannot inherit the survivorship right, which existed only between the original parties.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Estates and Interests)

questions.prompt: To establish title by adverse possession in New York, the possession must be:
choices: Hostile, actual, open and notorious, exclusive, and continuous for ten years
Permissive, continuous, and documented for ten years
Hostile and continuous for five years with payment of taxes
Open and continuous for twenty-one years
questions.explanation: Hostile means without the owner's permission. Permission defeats the claim entirely, which is why owners of land crossed by neighbors often grant a written license.

questions.prompt: A government action that so restricts the use of private land that it destroys the property's value may give rise to a claim of:
choices: Inverse condemnation, seeking compensation for a regulatory taking
Adverse possession against the municipality
Escheat, returning the land to the state
Novation of the underlying deed
questions.explanation: In ordinary condemnation the government initiates proceedings and pays. In inverse condemnation the owner sues, arguing that regulation amounted to a taking without compensation.

questions.prompt: In a New York residential closing, the buyer's attorney typically:
choices: Reviews the title report and clears objections before the closing date
Issues the title insurance policy on behalf of the underwriter
Performs the appraisal required by the lender
Files the certificate of occupancy with the building department
questions.explanation: New York closings are attorney-driven. Reviewing the title report and resolving exceptions is central to the buyer's attorney's role.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Title Closing and Costs)

questions.prompt: Under federal rules, a borrower must receive the Closing Disclosure for a covered residential mortgage at least:
choices: 3 business days before consummation
1 business day before consummation
7 business days before consummation
10 business days before consummation
questions.explanation: The three-day window exists so borrowers can compare the final figures to the Loan Estimate. Certain changes, such as an increased APR, restart the clock.

questions.prompt: Items on a closing statement shown as a credit to the buyer include:
choices: The earnest money deposit already paid
The purchase price of the property
The buyer's share of prepaid taxes
The title insurance premium the buyer owes
questions.explanation: The deposit is money the buyer has already delivered, so it reduces what remains due at closing. The purchase price and buyer-owed costs are debits.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Title Closing and Costs)

questions.prompt: A title insurance commitment's schedule of exceptions lists:
choices: Matters the policy will not cover, such as recorded easements and restrictions
The prior owners in the chain of title
The liens the seller must pay off before closing
The endorsements the lender has requested
questions.explanation: Exceptions carve items out of coverage. Reviewing them is how a buyer learns what easements, covenants, and survey matters they are taking the property subject to.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Title Closing and Costs)

questions.prompt: The New York form filed with the county clerk to report a real property transfer for assessment and sales-data purposes is:
choices: The RP-5217 Real Property Transfer Report
The TP-584 Combined Real Estate Transfer Tax Return
The DOS-1736 Agency Disclosure Form
The RPAPL Notice of Pendency
questions.explanation: The RP-5217 feeds assessment and sales data; the TP-584 is the separate transfer tax return. Both are typically filed at the same time as the deed.

questions.prompt: A survey is ordered before closing chiefly to reveal:
choices: Boundary lines, encroachments, and the location of improvements
Recorded liens against the property
The condition of the roof and mechanical systems
Whether the seller holds marketable title
questions.explanation: A survey shows physical facts on the ground that no records search can produce. Title policies commonly except survey matters unless a current survey is provided.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Title Closing and Costs)

questions.prompt: New York's homestead exemption operates to:
choices: Protect a portion of a primary residence's value from certain creditors
Reduce the assessed value of the property for school tax purposes
Exempt the first sale of a residence from transfer tax
Prevent a spouse from conveying the residence without consent
questions.explanation: The exemption is a creditor protection with a dollar amount that varies by county. STAR is the separate program that reduces school taxes.

questions.prompt: A fee simple estate that automatically ends if a stated condition occurs, such as land conveyed "so long as it is used as a library," is:
choices: A fee simple determinable, leaving the grantor a possibility of reverter
A fee simple absolute, since the condition is unenforceable
A life estate measured by the use of the property
A leasehold estate for an indefinite term
questions.explanation: The estate ends by itself when the condition fails, and the grantor's future interest is a possibility of reverter. Wording like "but if" instead creates a right of re-entry that must be exercised.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Legal Issues (Estates and Interests)

questions.prompt: A property has potential gross income of $200,000, vacancy and collection loss of 8%, and operating expenses of $70,000. Its net operating income is:
questions.explanation: Effective gross income is $200,000 less 8%, or $184,000. Subtracting $70,000 of operating expenses leaves $114,000.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: An investor buys a building for $1,200,000 that produces $96,000 in net operating income. The capitalization rate is:
questions.explanation: Cap rate is NOI divided by value: $96,000 / $1,200,000 = 8%.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: Under a gross lease, the landlord is generally responsible for:
choices: Property taxes, insurance, and maintenance, paid out of the rent received
Only the structural elements of the building
Nothing beyond delivering possession of the premises
Taxes only, with the tenant covering insurance and maintenance
questions.explanation: The tenant pays a single rent figure and the landlord absorbs operating costs. Escalation clauses are how landlords protect themselves against rising expenses.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: An escalation clause in a commercial lease allows the landlord to:
choices: Increase rent as specified operating costs rise during the lease term
Terminate the lease if the tenant's sales fall below a threshold
Recapture the space if a better tenant is found
Require the tenant to purchase the building at a set price
questions.explanation: Escalations pass through increases in taxes, insurance, or a published index, and are what make a long gross lease workable for a landlord.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A sale-leaseback transaction is typically motivated by the seller's desire to:
choices: Free capital tied up in real estate while continuing to occupy the property
Transfer management responsibility while retaining ownership
Defer capital gain under Section 1031
Obtain a mortgage without a personal guarantee
questions.explanation: The occupant converts an owned asset into cash and becomes a tenant. It is a financing decision as much as a real estate one.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A tenant leases 2,500 square feet at $28 per square foot per year. Monthly base rent is:
questions.explanation: Annual rent is 2,500 x $28 = $70,000. Divided by twelve months, monthly rent is $5,833.33.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: Rentable square footage differs from usable square footage because rentable includes:
choices: The tenant's proportionate share of building common areas
The area occupied by the tenant's own demising walls only
Parking spaces allocated to the tenant
Storage space in the building's basement
questions.explanation: The ratio between them is the load or add-on factor. Two quoted rents are not comparable unless you know which measure each uses.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A percentage lease sets a breakpoint, which is the sales level at which:
choices: Percentage rent begins to be owed on top of base rent
The landlord may terminate the lease for underperformance
The tenant's common area charges are capped
The lease automatically renews for another term
questions.explanation: Below the breakpoint the tenant pays base rent alone. A natural breakpoint is base rent divided by the percentage rate.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A tenant improvement allowance in a commercial lease is:
choices: A sum the landlord contributes toward building out the tenant's space
A rent credit for the months the tenant cannot occupy the space
A reduction in the tenant's share of common area charges
A deposit the tenant provides to secure future alterations
questions.explanation: Allowances are a negotiated concession alongside free rent. The effective rent over the term matters more than the headline rate once concessions are counted.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A subordination, non-disturbance and attornment agreement protects a commercial tenant by providing that:
choices: The lease survives a foreclosure of the landlord's mortgage
The tenant may terminate if the landlord defaults on the mortgage
The tenant's rent cannot increase during the lease term
The lender will fund the tenant's improvement allowance
questions.explanation: The tenant subordinates to the mortgage and agrees to recognize a new owner, in exchange for the lender's promise not to terminate the lease on foreclosure.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A Phase I environmental site assessment on a commercial acquisition primarily involves:
choices: Records review, a site visit, and interviews, with no sampling
Soil and groundwater sampling to confirm contamination
Remediation of any contamination discovered
An appraisal adjusted for environmental risk
questions.explanation: Phase I looks for recognized environmental conditions without testing. Phase II is where sampling happens, if Phase I gives reason for it.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: Conducting all appropriate inquiry before acquiring commercial property matters because it can establish:
choices: The innocent landowner defense to CERCLA liability
A lien priority over prior recorded mortgages
An exemption from local zoning requirements
Eligibility for a Section 1031 exchange
questions.explanation: CERCLA liability is strict and reaches current owners who caused nothing. The defense depends on having investigated properly before buying.
questions.citation: 42 U.S.C. §9601; DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: An investor's before-tax cash flow is calculated by subtracting from net operating income:
choices: Annual debt service
Depreciation
Operating expenses
Vacancy and collection loss
questions.explanation: NOI is already net of operating expenses and vacancy. Taking out debt service produces the cash the investor actually receives before income taxes.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: Two identical properties differ only in that one carries a long lease to a national credit tenant. That property will typically command:
choices: A lower capitalization rate, and therefore a higher price
A higher capitalization rate, and therefore a higher price
A lower capitalization rate, and therefore a lower price
The same capitalization rate, since the buildings are identical
questions.explanation: A more secure income stream lowers the required return. Cap rate and price move inversely, so a lower rate on the same NOI means a higher value.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A property's break-even ratio measures:
choices: The occupancy level at which income covers operating expenses and debt service
The ratio of a property's debt to its market value
The share of net operating income consumed by capital expenditures
The point at which appreciation offsets accumulated depreciation
questions.explanation: Also called the default ratio, it tells an investor how much the property can afford to sit empty before it stops paying for itself.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A property with $60,000 in net operating income is offered at a price that produces a 7.5% capitalization rate. The asking price is:
questions.explanation: Value equals NOI divided by cap rate: $60,000 / 0.075 = $800,000.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: In evaluating an apartment building, an investor treats an allowance for periodic roof and boiler replacement as:
choices: A reserve for replacements, an above-the-line deduction in arriving at NOI
A capital expenditure excluded from the operating statement entirely
Part of annual debt service
A financing cost deducted after NOI
questions.explanation: Including a replacement reserve produces a more honest NOI. A seller's statement that omits it will overstate income and therefore value.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: Class A office space is generally understood to mean buildings that are:
choices: The most prestigious in a market, commanding the highest rents
Newly constructed, regardless of location or rent level
Occupied entirely by a single corporate tenant
Owned by an institutional investor such as a pension fund
questions.explanation: The classification is relative to each market rather than absolute. Class A in a small city may be Class B in Manhattan.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A recapture clause in a retail lease permits the landlord to:
choices: Take back the space if the tenant's sales fail to reach a stated level
Recover unamortized tenant improvement costs at lease end
Increase base rent when comparable rents rise
Require the tenant to restore the premises to their original condition
questions.explanation: Recapture protects a landlord whose return depends on percentage rent from an underperforming tenant occupying valuable space.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A commercial property's loan-to-value ratio is 70% on a $2,000,000 purchase. The required equity is:
questions.explanation: A 70% loan is $1,400,000, leaving $600,000 of equity. Commercial lending typically requires more equity than residential.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A right of first refusal held by a commercial tenant allows the tenant to:
choices: Match the terms of a bona fide offer the landlord is prepared to accept
Purchase the property at a price fixed when the lease was signed
Prevent the landlord from selling during the lease term
Require the landlord to sell whenever the tenant chooses
questions.explanation: A right of first refusal is reactive, triggered by a third-party offer. An option to purchase, by contrast, lets the tenant initiate at a set price.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: In a triple net investment, the capitalization rate a buyer accepts depends most heavily on:
choices: The creditworthiness of the tenant and the remaining lease term
The replacement cost of the building
The age of the roof and mechanical systems
The property's assessed value for tax purposes
questions.explanation: With the tenant carrying operating costs, the investment is effectively a bond backed by that tenant. The tenant's credit becomes the dominant variable.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A holdover tenant in a commercial building is one who:
choices: Remains in possession after the lease term expires
Occupies space under a lease assigned from another tenant
Leases space month to month from the outset
Subleases a portion of its premises to a third party
questions.explanation: Commercial leases commonly impose holdover rent at 150% or 200% of the prior rate, because a holdover can prevent the landlord from delivering space to an incoming tenant.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: The internal rate of return on a real estate investment accounts for:
choices: The timing of all cash flows, including the eventual sale proceeds
Only the first year's cash flow relative to the purchase price
Net operating income before any financing
The ratio of gross rent to purchase price
questions.explanation: IRR discounts every projected cash flow to present value. It is the tool that distinguishes an investment paying off early from one paying off at sale.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A due diligence period in a commercial purchase contract exists so the buyer can:
choices: Investigate the property and terminate without penalty if it proves unsuitable
Arrange financing after the closing date has passed
Require the seller to complete deferred maintenance
Market the property to potential subtenants before closing
questions.explanation: The buyer typically has an unrestricted right to walk during this window, often with a refundable deposit. After it expires the deposit usually goes hard.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A tenant mix strategy in a shopping center aims to:
choices: Assemble complementary tenants whose customers overlap and reinforce each other
Lease to as many tenants in the same category as possible
Fill every space regardless of tenant type to eliminate vacancy
Reserve the largest spaces for the highest per-square-foot rents
questions.explanation: Center performance depends on the whole roster, not each lease in isolation. This is why leases often restrict competing uses.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: An exclusive use clause in a retail lease:
choices: Bars the landlord from leasing other space in the center to a competing use
Requires the tenant to use the space only for the stated purpose
Gives the tenant exclusive access to the center's parking
Prevents the tenant from subleasing any part of the premises
questions.explanation: It binds the landlord, not the tenant. A use clause is the separate provision limiting what the tenant may do in the space.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A property is appraised at $1,500,000 and carries a $900,000 mortgage. Its loan-to-value ratio is:
questions.explanation: $900,000 / $1,500,000 = 60%. Lenders use the lower of appraised value or purchase price when the two differ.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A general partner in a real estate limited partnership differs from the limited partners in that the general partner:
choices: Manages the venture and bears unlimited liability
Contributes the majority of the capital
Receives distributions before any limited partner
May not hold an ownership interest in the property
questions.explanation: The trade is control for exposure. Limited partners keep liability capped at their contribution but give up management authority.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: The primary appeal of a real estate investment trust to a small investor is:
choices: Liquidity and diversification without direct property management
The ability to depreciate the underlying real estate personally
Exemption from tax on distributions received
Direct control over which properties are acquired
questions.explanation: Publicly traded REIT shares can be sold in a day, which direct ownership never allows. Distributions are generally taxable to the shareholder.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: Absorption rate in a commercial market measures:
choices: The rate at which available space is leased over a period
The share of a building's income consumed by operating costs
The speed at which a property depreciates for tax purposes
The percentage of a loan repaid annually
questions.explanation: Net absorption compares space leased against space vacated. Negative absorption means a market is emptying faster than it fills.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A feasibility study for a proposed development primarily asks whether:
choices: The project can be built and operated profitably given market and cost conditions
The site complies with the current zoning ordinance
The developer can obtain title insurance for the parcel
The property's assessed value supports the expected tax burden
questions.explanation: Feasibility joins market demand, construction cost, financing, and regulatory constraints into one question about whether the project works.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: An industrial property's clear height refers to:
choices: The unobstructed vertical distance from floor to the lowest overhead obstruction
The height of the building measured from grade to roofline
The maximum height permitted by the zoning ordinance
The distance from the loading dock to the ceiling
questions.explanation: Clear height governs how high goods can be racked, which is why modern distribution tenants treat it as a threshold requirement.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A mixed-use development is one that:
choices: Combines two or more uses, such as residential over ground-floor retail
Permits any use allowed anywhere in the municipality
Contains both owner-occupied and rental units
Is financed by a combination of debt and equity
questions.explanation: Mixed use often requires a planned unit development or a special district, since conventional zoning separates uses by right.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: A commercial mortgage with a balloon payment requires the borrower to:
choices: Repay a large remaining principal balance at the end of the term
Make interest-only payments for the entire term
Increase payments annually according to an index
Pay a penalty if the loan is repaid early
questions.explanation: Payments are calculated on a longer amortization than the actual term, so a substantial balance remains due and typically must be refinanced.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: An investor comparing two properties finds identical cap rates but very different operating expense ratios. This most likely signals:
choices: A difference in lease structure, expense reporting, or deferred maintenance worth investigating
An arithmetic error, since cap rate and expense ratio must move together
That the property with the higher ratio is necessarily the better buy
That one property has a below-market mortgage in place
questions.explanation: A net-leased property shows a low expense ratio because tenants pay costs directly. An unusually low ratio can also mean a seller omitted expenses.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Commercial and Investment Properties

questions.prompt: The federal Fair Housing Act's seven protected classes are race, color, religion, national origin, sex, disability, and:
choices: Familial status
Marital status
Age
Source of income
questions.explanation: Familial status protects households with children under 18 and pregnant people. Marital status, age, and source of income are New York additions, not federal ones.

questions.prompt: New York's Human Rights Law protects several classes beyond the federal list, including:
choices: Age, marital status, military status, and sexual orientation
Occupation, education level, and credit score
Length of residence and employment history
Homeownership history and prior landlord references
questions.explanation: New York's list is substantially broader than the federal one, and New York City's Human Rights Law adds further categories on top of the state's.

questions.prompt: A landlord tells a tenant with a visual impairment that no pets are allowed and refuses a guide dog. This is:
choices: A failure to make a reasonable accommodation
A permissible enforcement of a uniform building policy
A refusal of a reasonable modification, which the tenant must fund
Permissible if the building has fewer than four units
questions.explanation: Service and assistance animals are not pets for fair housing purposes. Waiving a no-pets rule is the standard example of a reasonable accommodation.
questions.citation: 42 U.S.C. §3604(f); DOS 77-hour curriculum § Human Rights and Fair Housing

questions.prompt: A landlord may lawfully require a tenant who installed a wheelchair ramp to:
choices: Restore the premises to their original condition at the end of the tenancy, where reasonable
Pay a higher security deposit because of the disability
Provide medical documentation of the specific diagnosis
Relocate to a ground-floor unit designated for accessible use
questions.explanation: Restoration may be required for modifications where it is reasonable. Charging more, demanding a diagnosis, or steering to designated units are all violations.
questions.citation: 42 U.S.C. §3604(f); DOS 77-hour curriculum § Human Rights and Fair Housing

questions.prompt: Multifamily buildings of four or more units built for first occupancy after March 13, 1991 must meet:
choices: The Fair Housing Act's design and construction accessibility requirements
Title III of the Americans with Disabilities Act
The Architectural Barriers Act
Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, regardless of funding
questions.explanation: These requirements cover accessible routes, usable doors, and reinforced bathroom walls. ADA Title III governs public accommodations, not private residential units.

questions.prompt: A licensee is asked by a buyer about the racial composition of a neighborhood. The licensee should:
choices: Decline to characterize the neighborhood and point to publicly available census data
Answer honestly based on personal observation
Provide the information only if the buyer puts the request in writing
Show the buyer homes only in demographically similar neighborhoods
questions.explanation: Answering invites a steering claim regardless of intent. Directing the buyer to objective public sources lets them research without the licensee influencing the choice.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Human Rights and Fair Housing

questions.prompt: A person who believes they have suffered housing discrimination may file a complaint with HUD generally within:
choices: One year of the alleged discriminatory act
Thirty days of the alleged discriminatory act
Six months of the alleged discriminatory act
Three years of the alleged discriminatory act
questions.explanation: The administrative window with HUD is one year. A separate federal civil action carries a longer period, and state remedies run on their own timetables.

questions.prompt: In New York, a complaint alleging housing discrimination may be filed with:
choices: The New York State Division of Human Rights
The Department of State, Division of Licensing Services only
The New York State Board of Real Estate
The county clerk where the property is located
questions.explanation: The Division of Human Rights enforces the Human Rights Law. The Department of State separately disciplines the license of a licensee involved.
questions.citation: Executive Law Article 15; DOS 77-hour curriculum § Human Rights and Fair Housing

questions.prompt: The New York Department of State's Fair Housing Enforcement Program conducts:
choices: Undercover testing of rental and sale transactions to detect discriminatory treatment
Annual audits of every brokerage's transaction records
Mandatory mediation of all discrimination complaints
Pre-approval review of brokerage advertising
questions.explanation: The program grew out of documented steering in New York. Findings can lead to license discipline as well as human rights proceedings.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Human Rights and Fair Housing

questions.prompt: A landlord's blanket policy of refusing to rent to anyone with any criminal record may violate fair housing law because it:
choices: Can have a disparate impact on protected classes without any discriminatory intent
Is expressly prohibited by the federal protected class list
Constitutes steering under the Fair Housing Act
Amounts to blockbusting in neighborhoods undergoing change
questions.explanation: Disparate impact reaches neutral policies that fall more harshly on protected groups. Individualized assessment of the offense, its recency, and its relevance is the safer approach.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Human Rights and Fair Housing

questions.prompt: A New York licensee's continuing education must include a minimum number of hours on cultural competency. That minimum is:
choices: 2 hours
1 hour
3 hours
5 hours
questions.explanation: The cultural competency requirement, like the two-hour implicit bias requirement, came from the December 2021 legislative package on housing discrimination.

questions.prompt: Continuing education must include a minimum of how many hours on fair housing and discrimination?
choices: 3 hours
1 hour
2 hours
5 hours
questions.explanation: Fair housing carries the largest single required component of the 22.5-hour renewal requirement.

questions.prompt: The federal exemption sometimes called the Mrs. Murphy exemption applies to:
choices: An owner-occupied dwelling of four units or fewer, rented without a broker or discriminatory advertising
Any single-family home sold by its owner
Any building constructed before 1968
Housing owned by a religious organization or private club
questions.explanation: The exemption is narrow and evaporates the moment a licensee is used or discriminatory advertising appears. Race discrimination remains prohibited regardless under 42 U.S.C. §1981-1982.

questions.prompt: Even where a Fair Housing Act exemption applies, discrimination on the basis of race remains prohibited by:
choices: The Civil Rights Act of 1866, which has no exemptions
The Americans with Disabilities Act
The Equal Credit Opportunity Act
The Community Reinvestment Act
questions.explanation: Jones v. Alfred H. Mayer Co. confirmed the 1866 Act reaches all property transactions. It is the reason no exemption ever covers racial discrimination.
questions.citation: 42 U.S.C. §1982; Jones v. Alfred H. Mayer Co. (1968)

questions.prompt: A licensee is asked by an owner to market a property only through channels reaching a single ethnic community. The licensee should:
choices: Refuse, because limiting marketing that way denies information to protected classes
Comply, since the owner directs the marketing plan
Comply if the licensee also lists the property in the MLS
Comply but note the instruction in the transaction file
questions.explanation: Selective marketing achieves the same result as steering. The instruction is unlawful, and the duty of obedience does not extend to unlawful instructions.
questions.citation: 42 U.S.C. §3604(c); DOS 77-hour curriculum § Human Rights and Fair Housing

questions.prompt: The Equal Credit Opportunity Act prohibits discrimination in:
choices: The extension of credit, including on the basis of receipt of public assistance
The sale of residential property only
The rental of dwellings with more than four units
The provision of homeowner's insurance
questions.explanation: ECOA covers credit rather than housing directly, and its protected characteristics include age, marital status, and receipt of public assistance income.

questions.prompt: A New York licensee must provide the Housing and Anti-Discrimination Disclosure Form and:
choices: Retain proof that it was provided for at least three years
File a copy with the Division of Human Rights
Obtain the consumer's notarized signature
Provide it only to buyers, not to sellers or tenants
questions.explanation: The form goes to buyers, sellers, tenants, and landlords alike at first substantive contact, and retention follows the general three-year records rule.

questions.prompt: A non-solicitation order issued by the New York Secretary of State:
choices: Prohibits licensees from soliciting listings within a designated geographic area
Prevents any property in the area from being sold for a stated period
Requires licensees to obtain written consent before advertising in the area
Bars new brokerages from opening offices in the area
questions.explanation: Non-solicitation orders respond to blockbusting activity in a defined area. Violating one is grounds for license discipline.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Human Rights and Fair Housing

questions.prompt: A brokerage's advertisement featuring only images of one racial group in a diverse market may:
choices: Suggest a preference and violate the Fair Housing Act's advertising provisions
Be permissible, since images are not statements of preference
Be permissible if a fair housing logo appears in the advertisement
Violate antitrust law rather than fair housing law
questions.explanation: Human models in advertising should reasonably represent the market. The test is the message conveyed to an ordinary reader, not the advertiser's intent.
questions.citation: 42 U.S.C. §3604(c); DOS 77-hour curriculum § Human Rights and Fair Housing

questions.prompt: The New York State Human Rights Law's protection for domestic violence victim status means a landlord may not:
choices: Refuse to rent because the applicant has been a victim of domestic violence
Ask any applicant for references from a prior landlord
Require any applicant to provide proof of income
Enforce a lease provision limiting overnight guests
questions.explanation: New York added this protection to stop applicants being penalized for police activity or lease terminations connected to abuse they suffered.

questions.prompt: For housing to qualify under the older persons exemption to familial status, one common standard requires that:
choices: At least 80% of occupied units have a resident 55 or older, with published policies demonstrating intent
Every resident be at least 62 years of age without exception
The property be operated by a government agency
The property contain no more than four dwelling units
questions.explanation: The 55-and-older route requires the 80% occupancy standard plus published policies and age verification. A separate route requires all occupants be 62 or older.

questions.prompt: A licensee who follows a seller's discriminatory instruction is:
choices: Personally liable, and also exposed to license discipline
Shielded from liability because the seller gave the instruction
Liable only if the licensee profited from the transaction
Liable only if the affected buyer files suit within thirty days
questions.explanation: Agency does not transfer liability for unlawful acts. Both the principal and the licensee who carries out the instruction can be held responsible.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Human Rights and Fair Housing

questions.prompt: The purpose of the anti-bias training component added to New York's qualifying curriculum is to address:
choices: Unconscious stereotypes that can influence how licensees treat consumers
Deliberate refusals to show property to protected classes
Advertising practices in print and digital media
Recordkeeping requirements for agency disclosure forms
questions.explanation: The component targets treatment differences a licensee may not recognize in themselves, which testing has repeatedly documented in New York.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Human Rights and Fair Housing

questions.prompt: A property manager applies a minimum income requirement of 40 times the monthly rent, but counts only wage income and excludes housing vouchers. In New York this is:
choices: Likely unlawful, because it discriminates on the basis of lawful source of income
Lawful, because income standards are applied to every applicant equally
Lawful, because vouchers are paid to the landlord rather than the tenant
Unlawful only in buildings receiving public subsidy
questions.explanation: A facially neutral income test applied so that voucher holders can never qualify is a common form of source of income discrimination.

questions.prompt: In an amortized mortgage, the portion of each monthly payment allocated to interest:
choices: Decreases over the life of the loan as the principal balance falls
Remains constant throughout the loan term
Increases over the life of the loan
Is recalculated annually based on the property's value
questions.explanation: Interest is charged on the outstanding balance. Early payments are mostly interest; later ones are mostly principal, even though the total payment does not change.

questions.prompt: A borrower's loan has a balance of $240,000 at 6% annual interest. The interest portion of the next monthly payment is:
questions.explanation: Annual interest is $240,000 x 0.06 = $14,400. One month's share is $14,400 / 12 = $1,200.

questions.prompt: The secondary mortgage market exists primarily to:
choices: Buy loans from originating lenders, replenishing funds available for new lending
Make second mortgages available to homeowners
Insure lenders against borrower default
Set the interest rates lenders may charge
questions.explanation: Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and Ginnie Mae operate here. Their underwriting standards effectively set the terms of conventional conforming lending.

questions.prompt: A conforming loan is one that:
choices: Meets the size and underwriting standards for purchase by Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac
Is insured by the Federal Housing Administration
Carries a fixed rate for its entire term
Requires no private mortgage insurance
questions.explanation: Loans above the limit are jumbo loans, which lenders must hold or sell privately, and which therefore usually price differently.

questions.prompt: A VA-guaranteed loan differs from an FHA-insured loan in that the VA loan:
choices: Guarantees a portion of the loan and commonly requires no down payment
Insures the entire loan amount against default
Is available to any borrower meeting the income limits
Is originated directly by the Department of Veterans Affairs
questions.explanation: The VA guarantees part of the loan, which is why qualified veterans can often borrow with nothing down. Neither agency lends directly.

questions.prompt: In an adjustable rate mortgage, the margin is:
choices: The fixed percentage the lender adds to the index to set the rate
The maximum the rate may increase in any single adjustment
The difference between the initial rate and the fully indexed rate
The lender's profit on the sale of the loan
questions.explanation: The index moves with the market; the margin stays fixed for the life of the loan. Caps are the separate limits on how far the rate may move.

questions.prompt: A mortgage taken by a buyer from the seller as part of the purchase price is:
choices: A purchase money mortgage
A wraparound mortgage
A blanket mortgage
A package mortgage
questions.explanation: Seller financing is the common form. Purchase money mortgages generally take priority over other liens arising against the buyer at the same time.

questions.prompt: A blanket mortgage is one that:
choices: Covers more than one parcel, typically with a release clause for individual lots
Includes personal property along with the real estate
Wraps around an existing mortgage that remains in place
Adjusts its rate according to a published index
questions.explanation: Developers use blanket mortgages to finance subdivisions. The partial release clause lets individual lots be sold free of the lien as they close.

questions.prompt: A package mortgage differs from an ordinary mortgage because it:
choices: Secures personal property such as appliances along with the real estate
Covers several separate parcels under one lien
Permits the borrower to draw additional funds after closing
Requires no monthly payment until the balloon date
questions.explanation: Package mortgages are common in furnished condominium and resort sales, where the fixtures and contents are financed with the unit.

questions.prompt: New York requires foreclosure of a residential mortgage to proceed:
choices: Through the courts, as a judicial foreclosure
By power of sale, without court involvement
By the lender taking possession after a 30-day notice
Through the Department of Financial Services
questions.explanation: As a lien theory, judicial foreclosure state, New York requires a lawsuit. Borrowers also receive statutory pre-foreclosure notices and a settlement conference.
questions.citation: RPAPL Article 13; DOS 77-hour curriculum § Real Estate Finance

questions.prompt: A borrower's equity of redemption is the right to:
choices: Pay the full debt and reclaim the property before the foreclosure sale
Force the lender to accept a deed in lieu of foreclosure
Remain in possession for one year after the sale
Recover the property from the purchaser after the sale has closed
questions.explanation: The right runs until the sale extinguishes it. Some states add a statutory right of redemption after the sale; New York does not provide one for mortgage foreclosures.

questions.prompt: A short sale occurs when:
choices: The lender agrees to accept less than the balance owed to permit a sale
A property sells within thirty days of listing
The buyer assumes the seller's existing mortgage
The lender forecloses and sells at public auction
questions.explanation: The lender's approval is what makes the transaction possible, which is why short sales take far longer than ordinary ones and can fall apart late.

questions.prompt: A deficiency judgment may be sought by a lender when:
choices: The foreclosure sale proceeds are less than the debt owed
The borrower prepays the loan before its maturity date
The property appraises below the purchase price
The borrower fails to maintain hazard insurance
questions.explanation: The judgment covers the shortfall and becomes a general lien against the borrower's other property. Availability is limited by statute in various circumstances.

questions.prompt: A subordination clause in a mortgage provides that:
choices: The lien will take a lower priority position to a later-recorded mortgage
The borrower may not place additional liens on the property
The lender may accelerate the debt upon a sale of the property
The loan may be assumed by a qualified buyer
questions.explanation: Subordination is common in land acquisition, where the seller agrees to step behind a construction lender so the project can be financed.

questions.prompt: A defeasance clause in a mortgage operates to:
choices: Require the lender to release the lien when the debt is fully paid
Allow the lender to declare the entire balance due on default
Prevent the borrower from prepaying without penalty
Permit the loan to be transferred to a new borrower
questions.explanation: Recording the satisfaction of mortgage is what actually clears the record. An unreleased paid mortgage is a common cloud on title.

questions.prompt: A buyer who takes title subject to an existing mortgage, rather than assuming it:
choices: Does not become personally liable for the debt
Becomes primarily liable for the debt
Releases the original borrower from all liability
Must obtain the lender's written approval in every case
questions.explanation: The buyer risks losing the property to foreclosure but owes nothing personally. Assumption makes the buyer liable; a novation is required to release the seller.

questions.prompt: A lender's requirement that a borrower escrow funds monthly for taxes and insurance produces:
choices: A PITI payment covering principal, interest, taxes, and insurance
A reduction in the loan's annual percentage rate
An increase in the borrower's equity each month
