A waiver of the private mortgage insurance requirement
questions.explanation: Escrowing protects the lender's collateral by ensuring taxes and coverage stay current, since a tax lien would otherwise outrank the mortgage.

questions.prompt: The front-end qualifying ratio a lender applies compares:
choices: Housing expense to gross monthly income
Total monthly debt to gross monthly income
Loan amount to appraised value
Net operating income to annual debt service
questions.explanation: The back-end ratio adds all recurring debt. Both must satisfy the lender, and the back-end ratio is usually the binding constraint.

questions.prompt: A borrower has gross monthly income of $8,000 and the lender applies a 28% front-end ratio. The maximum monthly housing expense is:
questions.explanation: $8,000 x 0.28 = $2,240, covering principal, interest, taxes, and insurance together.

questions.prompt: Usury laws limit:
choices: The maximum interest rate a lender may charge
The maximum term a mortgage loan may run
The number of points a lender may collect
The fees a mortgage broker may charge a borrower
questions.explanation: New York sets civil and criminal usury ceilings, with exemptions for certain loan types and amounts. Charging above the limit can cost a lender the interest or the whole debt.

questions.prompt: Under the federal lead-based paint rule, a purchaser of pre-1978 housing must be given an opportunity to conduct a risk assessment lasting:
choices: 10 days, unless the parties agree otherwise
3 days
30 days
5 business days
questions.explanation: The seller must also disclose known hazards, provide any available reports, and deliver the EPA pamphlet. The ten-day period is the default and can be varied by agreement.

questions.prompt: A brownfield site differs from a Superfund site in that a brownfield is:
choices: A property whose redevelopment is complicated by possible contamination, often eligible for cleanup incentives
A site already listed on the National Priorities List
A property contaminated only by petroleum products
Land that has never been developed
questions.explanation: Brownfield programs, including New York's, offer tax credits and liability relief to encourage redevelopment of moderately contaminated sites rather than greenfield land.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: An abandoned residential heating oil tank buried in the yard is a concern chiefly because:
choices: Leaking product can contaminate soil and groundwater, and remediation costs fall on the owner
It reduces the property's assessed value for tax purposes
Building codes require every tank to be replaced every ten years
It voids the property's title insurance coverage
questions.explanation: Discovery of an unregistered underground tank routinely derails closings, because the cost of testing and remediation is unpredictable.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: Development affecting a freshwater wetland in New York generally requires:
choices: A permit from the Department of Environmental Conservation
Approval from the Department of State's Division of Licensing Services
A variance from the local zoning board of appeals only
No approval, provided the parcel is under one acre
questions.explanation: Wetlands regulation is a common surprise on rural and waterfront parcels, and regulated adjacent areas extend the restriction beyond the wetland boundary itself.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: Mold growth in a dwelling is best addressed by:
choices: Correcting the underlying moisture source, then removing the affected material
Applying a fungicide and repainting the affected surface
Increasing the building's insulation R-value
Installing a radon mitigation system
questions.explanation: Mold is a symptom of a water problem. Remediation that does not fix the moisture source simply defers the recurrence.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: A vapor barrier installed in a wall assembly is intended to:
choices: Restrict moisture migration into the wall cavity
Increase the thermal resistance of the insulation
Provide structural rigidity to the framing
Block radon entry from the soil
questions.explanation: Placement matters: in a cold climate the barrier belongs on the warm side of the insulation, or it traps condensation inside the wall.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: In platform framing, the most common method in modern residential construction:
choices: Each floor is built as a platform on which the next storey's walls are framed
Wall studs run continuously from the foundation to the roof
Heavy timbers are joined with mortise and tenon connections
Load is carried by exterior masonry rather than a wood frame
questions.explanation: Platform framing uses shorter, more manageable studs and creates natural fire stops at each floor level, which is why it displaced balloon framing.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: A load-bearing wall is one that:
choices: Carries structural weight from above down to the foundation
Separates conditioned space from unconditioned space
Contains the building's plumbing and electrical runs
Forms the exterior envelope of the structure
questions.explanation: Removing one without engineered support is a serious defect. Buyers of renovated homes should confirm that structural alterations were permitted and inspected.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: A footing in residential construction serves to:
choices: Spread the building's load over a wider area of soil beneath the foundation wall
Prevent water from entering the basement
Anchor the sill plate to the foundation
Provide a level surface for the finished floor
questions.explanation: Footings must sit below the local frost line so seasonal freezing does not heave the foundation.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: Building construction in New York is governed principally by:
choices: The New York State Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code
The federal International Residential Code as adopted by HUD
Local ordinances alone, with no statewide standard
The building code of the county in which the property sits
questions.explanation: The Uniform Code sets a statewide floor. Municipalities administer and enforce it locally, and New York City operates its own code.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: Work performed without a required building permit creates a risk for a buyer because:
choices: The municipality can require the work to be opened for inspection or removed
The title insurer will refuse to issue any policy
The property automatically loses its certificate of occupancy
The seller's transfer tax obligation increases
questions.explanation: Unpermitted work also frequently blocks a lender's approval and surfaces later when the buyer tries to sell or to permit further work.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: The electrical service capacity of a home is measured in:
choices: Amperes
Volts
Watts
British thermal units
questions.explanation: Older homes with 60-amp service often cannot support modern loads. Upgrading to 200-amp service is a common condition of sale.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: Heating and cooling equipment capacity is commonly expressed in:
choices: British thermal units
Amperes
R-values
Kilowatt hours per square foot
questions.explanation: Correct sizing matters in both directions. Oversized equipment short-cycles, which wastes energy and fails to dehumidify properly.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: Flashing is installed on a roof to:
choices: Seal joints and penetrations against water intrusion
Provide ventilation to the attic space
Increase the roof's insulating value
Support the weight of accumulated snow
questions.explanation: Failed flashing around chimneys, valleys, and vents is a more common source of roof leaks than failure of the shingles themselves.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: Improper grading around a house most commonly results in:
choices: Water directed toward the foundation, causing basement moisture problems
Uneven settling of interior floor joists
Elevated radon levels in upper storeys
Ice damming along the roof eaves
questions.explanation: Soil should slope away from the foundation. Regrading and extending downspouts often resolve chronic basement water more cheaply than interior systems.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: A private well serving a residence should be tested before purchase primarily for:
choices: Bacteria such as coliform, along with nitrates and other local contaminants
Water pressure and flow rate only
Hardness and mineral content only
Radon in air, but not in water
questions.explanation: Coliform indicates surface contamination reaching the aquifer. Testing is not automatic in most transactions and must be requested.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: Radon mitigation in a home with elevated levels is most commonly accomplished by:
choices: Sub-slab depressurization, venting soil gas above the roofline
Sealing all basement windows permanently
Installing a whole-house dehumidifier
Encapsulating the basement floor with epoxy coating
questions.explanation: The system draws gas from beneath the slab before it can enter. Sealing cracks alone is rarely sufficient on its own.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: A home's septic system should generally be located:
choices: A regulated minimum distance from any well, property line, and water body
Directly beneath the driveway to minimize yard disruption
Within ten feet of the foundation wall
Anywhere on the lot, provided percolation is adequate
questions.explanation: Setback distances are set by health department rules. A failing system on a small lot may have nowhere to relocate, which can make the parcel unbuildable.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: Urea formaldehyde in a home is associated chiefly with:
choices: Off-gassing from certain insulation and pressed-wood products
Radioactive decay in soil beneath the foundation
Deteriorating pipe insulation in older basements
Lead solder used in plumbing joints
questions.explanation: Off-gassing declines over time, so the concern is greatest with newer materials. It is distinct from asbestos, radon, and lead, which have entirely different sources.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: A buyer's home inspection contingency differs from the Property Condition Disclosure Statement because the inspection:
choices: Is an independent professional examination, while the statement reflects only the seller's knowledge
Is required by statute in every New York residential transaction
Covers title defects as well as physical condition
Replaces the seller's disclosure obligation entirely
questions.explanation: The disclosure statement is limited to what the seller actually knows. Neither substitutes for the other, and buyers should not treat the statement as a condition report.
questions.citation: RPL Article 14; DOS 77-hour curriculum § Construction and Environmental Issues

questions.prompt: Limited common elements in a condominium are:
choices: Portions of the common elements reserved for the use of one or more specific units
Areas owned outright by the individual unit owner
Common areas the board may sell without unit owner consent
Parts of the building excluded from the declaration entirely
questions.explanation: A balcony reachable only from one unit, or a parking space assigned to it, are typical examples. They remain common elements but with exclusive use rights.
questions.citation: RPL Article 9-B; DOS 77-hour curriculum § Condominiums and Cooperatives

questions.prompt: A condominium unit owner's percentage of common interest determines:
choices: Their share of common charges and typically their voting power
The square footage of the unit they own
The number of parking spaces assigned to the unit
The order in which units may be resold
questions.explanation: The percentage is fixed in the declaration and generally reflects the unit's relative value at the time the condominium was created.

questions.prompt: A condominium board that must fund an unexpected facade repair will typically:
choices: Levy a special assessment against the unit owners
Increase the flip tax on future sales
Place a lien on the common elements
Petition the Attorney General to amend the offering plan
questions.explanation: A pending or rumored special assessment is a material fact in a resale, and buyers should ask about the reserve fund and any planned capital work.

questions.prompt: A cooperative shareholder's monthly maintenance payment typically includes:
choices: Their share of the building's underlying mortgage and real estate taxes
Only the cost of common area utilities and staffing
The shareholder's own share loan payment
Real estate taxes only, with debt service billed separately
questions.explanation: Because maintenance carries the building's blanket mortgage and taxes, co-op maintenance figures are not directly comparable to condominium common charges.

questions.prompt: A cooperative shareholder may generally deduct on their personal income tax return:
choices: Their proportionate share of the corporation's mortgage interest and real estate taxes
The entire monthly maintenance payment
Nothing, because the shareholder does not own real property
Only the portion of maintenance allocated to building staff
questions.explanation: The corporation reports each shareholder's proportionate share annually. The operating portion of maintenance is not deductible.

questions.prompt: A land lease cooperative differs from an ordinary co-op because the corporation:
choices: Leases rather than owns the land beneath the building
Is prohibited from placing an underlying mortgage on the property
Holds title to each apartment as a separate tax lot
May not require board approval of purchasers
questions.explanation: A ground lease approaching expiration or a large rent reset can sharply affect share values, which is why the lease term is a key diligence item.

questions.prompt: A sponsor in a New York condominium or cooperative conversion is:
choices: The party offering the units for sale under the accepted offering plan
The managing agent retained to operate the building
The attorney who files the plan with the Attorney General
The lender providing the building's underlying mortgage
questions.explanation: Sponsor-held unsold units matter to buyers and lenders, since heavy sponsor ownership can affect financing availability and board control.

questions.prompt: A homeowners association in a planned community differs from a condominium in that association members:
choices: Own their lots and homes in fee, with the association owning the common areas
Own shares in a corporation rather than real property
Hold an undivided interest in the common elements as tenants in common
Lease their homes from the association under a proprietary lease
questions.explanation: The association is a separate legal entity holding the common land. Membership and assessment obligations run with the lot through recorded covenants.

questions.prompt: A cooperative's board that wishes to restrict subletting generally derives that authority from:
choices: The proprietary lease and the corporation's bylaws
The Real Property Law's rent regulation provisions
The Attorney General's acceptance of the offering plan
The local municipality's zoning ordinance
questions.explanation: Sublet restrictions, fees, and waiting periods are common and are a material fact for a buyer intending to rent the unit out.

questions.prompt: A condominium's reserve fund exists to:
choices: Pay for major repairs and replacements without a special assessment
Cover the sponsor's obligations on unsold units
Guarantee the underlying mortgage against default
Refund common charges to owners at year end
questions.explanation: An underfunded reserve is a warning sign. Lenders reviewing a project's financials often look for a minimum share of the budget going to reserves.

questions.prompt: The document that legally creates a condominium and defines the units and common elements is the:
choices: Declaration, recorded in the county land records
Proprietary lease issued to each owner
Offering plan filed with the Attorney General
Certificate of incorporation of the board of managers
questions.explanation: The declaration plus the filed floor plans create the condominium regime. Bylaws govern operations, and the offering plan governs the initial sale.

questions.prompt: Unpaid common charges in a New York condominium give the board:
choices: A lien on the unit that can be foreclosed
The right to terminate the owner's occupancy as a defaulting tenant
Authority to sell the owner's shares at public auction
No remedy other than a personal lawsuit against the owner
questions.explanation: Because the unit is real property, the condominium remedy is a lien and foreclosure. A co-op instead terminates the proprietary lease and sells the shares.

questions.prompt: A purchaser of a co-op apartment finances the acquisition using:
choices: A share loan secured by the stock and the proprietary lease
A conventional mortgage recorded against the apartment
A blanket mortgage covering the entire building
A purchase money mortgage granted by the corporation
questions.explanation: The lender takes a security interest in personal property, perfected under the Uniform Commercial Code rather than by recording a mortgage.

questions.prompt: A recognition agreement in a cooperative transaction is executed among the:
choices: Lender, the shareholder, and the cooperative corporation
Buyer, the seller, and the managing agent
Corporation, the sponsor, and the Attorney General
Board of directors, the buyer, and the title insurer
questions.explanation: It defines what happens if the shareholder defaults, giving the lender notice and rights while confirming the corporation's priority for unpaid maintenance.

questions.prompt: A condominium unit differs from a cooperative apartment for property tax purposes because the condominium unit:
choices: Is separately assessed and taxed as its own tax lot
Is exempt from local property taxation
Is taxed as personal property rather than real property
Is assessed only when it is sold
questions.explanation: A co-op building is assessed as a single parcel and the tax flows through maintenance, which is why co-op owners do not receive individual tax bills.

questions.prompt: A buyer of a resale condominium unit should review the board's minutes and financial statements primarily to identify:
choices: Pending litigation, capital projects, and the adequacy of reserves
The identities of the other unit owners
The original sponsor's profit on the conversion
The assessed value of neighboring units
questions.explanation: Litigation and deferred capital work translate directly into future assessments. These documents are where those risks surface before closing.

questions.prompt: The qualifying course a New York salesperson applicant must complete runs:
choices: 77 hours
75 hours
60 hours
90 hours
questions.explanation: The requirement rose to 77 hours under the curriculum effective 12/21/2022. Older material citing 75 hours reflects the pre-2008 requirement.

questions.prompt: A passing New York salesperson examination result remains valid for:
choices: 2 years
1 year
3 years
5 years
questions.explanation: The license application must be filed within that window. Letting it lapse means retaking the examination.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § License Law and Regulations

questions.prompt: New York currently maintains real estate license reciprocity with:
choices: No other state
All states bordering New York
Any state whose requirements meet or exceed New York's
Only Pennsylvania and Connecticut
questions.explanation: New York's previous reciprocity agreements are no longer in effect. Many third-party sources still list them, which makes this a common source of confusion.
questions.citation: DOS salesperson FAQ; DOS 77-hour curriculum § License Law and Regulations

questions.prompt: A licensee whose license has expired may renew it late for a period of up to:
choices: 2 years after expiration
6 months after expiration
1 year after expiration
90 days after expiration
questions.explanation: Beyond that window the applicant must qualify as a new licensee. No brokerage activity may occur while the license is expired.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § License Law and Regulations

questions.prompt: The Department of State may revoke or suspend a license for:
choices: Demonstrated untrustworthiness or incompetence
Failing to close a minimum number of transactions each year
Advertising a property at a price the seller later rejects
Refusing to accept a listing from a prospective client
questions.explanation: Untrustworthiness is the broad standard the Department applies. It reaches conduct well beyond specific enumerated violations.

questions.prompt: A person who performs brokerage activity in New York without a license:
choices: Cannot maintain an action to collect a commission
May collect a commission if the client agreed to it in writing
May collect only the portion attributable to work performed
May collect through a licensed broker acting as intermediary
questions.explanation: The courthouse door is closed to unlicensed persons seeking compensation for brokerage services, regardless of the agreement or the value provided.

questions.prompt: Continuing education for renewal must include at least one hour on:
choices: Recent legal matters affecting real estate practice
Property management fundamentals
Real estate mathematics
Commercial lease negotiation
questions.explanation: The required components are fair housing, ethical business practices, implicit bias, cultural competency, recent legal matters, and law of agency.

questions.prompt: Continuing education must include a minimum of how many hours on ethical business practices?
choices: 2.5 hours
1 hour
3 hours
4 hours
questions.explanation: Ethical business practices carries a 2.5-hour minimum within the 22.5-hour renewal requirement.

questions.prompt: A broker maintaining a branch office in New York must:
choices: Obtain a separate branch office license and place it under a supervising licensee
Notify the Department of State within thirty days of opening
Register the office with the county clerk where it is located
Operate it under the main office license with no further filing
questions.explanation: Each branch requires its own license and its own supervision, which supports the broker's overall duty to supervise associated licensees.

questions.prompt: A licensee must disclose their licensed status when:
choices: Buying or selling property for their own account
Attending an open house hosted by another brokerage
Referring a friend to another licensee
Renewing their license with the Department of State
questions.explanation: The disclosure prevents a licensee from using professional knowledge against an unsuspecting party in a personal transaction.

questions.prompt: The Department of State's authority over licensees is exercised through:
choices: Administrative hearings that can result in fines, suspension, or revocation
Criminal prosecution in state supreme court
Binding arbitration administered by local real estate boards
Civil actions brought on behalf of aggrieved consumers
questions.explanation: A licensee dissatisfied with the outcome may seek judicial review through an Article 78 proceeding after exhausting the administrative process.

questions.prompt: An applicant for a New York salesperson license must be at least:
choices: 18 years of age
21 years of age
19 years of age
16 years of age
questions.explanation: Salesperson applicants must be 18; broker applicants must be 20 and must also satisfy an experience requirement.

questions.prompt: The essential elements of a valid contract are competent parties, lawful object, consideration, and:
choices: Offer and acceptance constituting mutual assent
A written instrument signed by both parties
Delivery of possession to the buyer
Recording in the county land records
questions.explanation: Writing is required for enforceability of real estate contracts under the statute of frauds, but it is not one of the elements that makes a contract valid.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § The Contract of Sales and Leases (Contracts)

questions.prompt: A buyer makes an offer and the seller returns it with a higher price. The seller's response is:
choices: A counteroffer, which terminates the buyer's original offer
An acceptance with a modification, binding both parties
A rejection that the buyer may still accept within three days
A conditional acceptance that becomes binding if the buyer is silent
questions.explanation: A counteroffer kills the original offer. The original offeror becomes the offeree and is free to accept, reject, or counter again.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § The Contract of Sales and Leases (Contracts)

questions.prompt: A buyer who breaches a purchase contract may face:
choices: Forfeiture of the down payment as liquidated damages, if the contract so provides
Automatic liability for the seller's full carrying costs until resale
Criminal penalties under the Real Property Law
A lien against the buyer's other real property
questions.explanation: Liquidated damages fix the remedy in advance and avoid litigating actual loss. A seller may alternatively sue for damages or specific performance where available.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § The Contract of Sales and Leases (Contracts)

questions.prompt: Specific performance is a remedy that compels:
choices: The breaching party to complete the transaction as agreed
The return of all deposits to the injured party
Payment of the difference between contract price and market value
Cancellation of the contract and restoration of the parties
questions.explanation: It is available because each parcel of land is considered unique, so money damages are treated as an inadequate substitute.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § The Contract of Sales and Leases (Contracts)

questions.prompt: A contract provision stating that time is of the essence means:
choices: Performance by the stated date is a material term, and delay is a breach
The parties intend to close as promptly as circumstances permit
Either party may extend the closing date once without penalty
The contract expires automatically if not recorded promptly
questions.explanation: Without such a clause, courts generally allow a reasonable adjournment. With it, missing the date can forfeit the deposit or the deal.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § The Contract of Sales and Leases (Contracts)

questions.prompt: A mortgage contingency clause in a residential contract permits the buyer to:
choices: Cancel and recover the deposit if a loan commitment cannot be obtained by the stated date
Reduce the purchase price if the appraisal comes in low
Extend the closing indefinitely while seeking financing
Assign the contract to another buyer who can obtain financing
questions.explanation: The buyer must generally apply in good faith and give timely notice. Missing the notice deadline can waive the contingency entirely.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § The Contract of Sales and Leases (Contracts)

questions.prompt: The substitution of a new party or obligation for an existing one, releasing the original party, is:
choices: A novation
An assignment
A rescission
A ratification
questions.explanation: An assignment transfers rights but generally leaves the assignor liable. Only a novation, requiring the obligee's consent, releases the original party.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § The Contract of Sales and Leases (Contracts)

questions.prompt: A lease for a fixed term with a definite beginning and ending date creates:
choices: An estate for years, which ends without notice
A periodic tenancy requiring notice to terminate
A tenancy at will terminable by either party at any time
A tenancy at sufferance
questions.explanation: The term need not be measured in years. What matters is that the ending date is fixed, so no notice is required to end it.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § The Contract of Sales and Leases (Leases)

questions.prompt: A tenant who remains in possession after a lease expires, without the landlord's consent, holds:
choices: A tenancy at sufferance
A tenancy at will
A periodic tenancy renewed automatically
An estate for years extended by operation of law
questions.explanation: A tenancy at sufferance is the lowest estate, distinguished from trespass only because possession began lawfully. Accepting rent can convert it into a periodic tenancy.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § The Contract of Sales and Leases (Leases)

questions.prompt: Actual eviction of a tenant in New York requires the landlord to:
choices: Obtain a court judgment and have a marshal or sheriff execute the warrant
Provide thirty days' written notice and change the locks
Remove the tenant's belongings after the rent is fifteen days late
Shut off utilities until the tenant vacates
questions.explanation: Self-help eviction, including lockouts and utility shutoffs, is unlawful. Only a court-ordered warrant executed by an enforcement officer can remove a tenant.

questions.prompt: Constructive eviction occurs when a landlord:
choices: Allows conditions so severe that the tenant is forced to vacate
Serves a notice to quit before the lease term ends
Refuses to renew the lease at its expiration
Increases the rent beyond what the tenant can afford
questions.explanation: The tenant must generally actually vacate to claim it. Remaining in possession while withholding rent is a different, and riskier, strategy.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § The Contract of Sales and Leases (Leases)

questions.prompt: An option to purchase gives the holder:
choices: The right, but not the obligation, to buy on stated terms within a stated period
An obligation to purchase if financing can be obtained
A right to match any offer the owner receives
An equitable lien against the property for the option price
questions.explanation: The optionee holds a unilateral right; the optionor is bound. Consideration must support the option itself for it to be enforceable.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § The Contract of Sales and Leases (Contracts)

questions.prompt: A comprehensive plan adopted by a municipality functions as:
choices: A long-range policy document that zoning is expected to implement
A binding regulation enforceable against individual property owners
A map of every parcel's assessed value
A schedule of permitted uses in each district
questions.explanation: Zoning that departs sharply from the comprehensive plan invites a legal challenge, which is why spot zoning is vulnerable.

questions.prompt: A use that a zoning ordinance allows in a district only after review and approval of its specific site and conditions requires:
choices: A special use permit
A use variance
An area variance
A zoning amendment
questions.explanation: The use is contemplated by the ordinance but needs conditions attached. A variance, by contrast, permits something the ordinance does not allow at all.

questions.prompt: To obtain a use variance, an applicant generally must demonstrate:
choices: Unnecessary hardship, including that the property cannot yield a reasonable return as zoned
That the proposed use would increase the property's assessed value
That a majority of neighbors do not object
That the existing use has been abandoned for over a year
questions.explanation: The burden is deliberately heavy. The hardship must arise from the property itself rather than from the owner's personal circumstances, and must not be self-created.

questions.prompt: A planned unit development is a zoning technique that:
choices: Allows mixed uses and flexible lot standards across a project treated as a whole
Restricts a district to a single residential density
Transfers development rights from one parcel to another
Exempts a project from environmental review
questions.explanation: PUDs let a developer cluster housing and preserve open space in exchange for negotiated site-wide standards rather than lot-by-lot compliance.

questions.prompt: A setback requirement in a zoning ordinance specifies:
choices: The minimum distance a structure must sit from a lot line
The maximum height a structure may reach
The share of a lot that may be covered by buildings
The minimum lot area required per dwelling unit
questions.explanation: Setbacks are dimensional requirements, which is why relief from them is sought through an area variance rather than a use variance.

questions.prompt: A subdivision regulation typically requires a developer to:
choices: Submit a plat for approval and install required infrastructure improvements
Obtain a use variance for each lot created
Convey a portion of the land to the state
Complete an environmental remediation before filing
questions.explanation: Approval conditions commonly include roads, drainage, and utilities, often secured by a performance bond until the work is finished.

questions.prompt: A discretionary action by a New York municipal agency that may significantly affect the environment triggers review under:
choices: The State Environmental Quality Review Act
CERCLA
The Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code
Article 78 of the Civil Practice Law and Rules
questions.explanation: SEQRA requires the agency to identify environmental impacts before approving an action, and can require a full environmental impact statement.
questions.citation: ECL Article 8; DOS 77-hour curriculum § Land Use Regulations

questions.prompt: A nonconforming use that is destroyed by fire may generally:
choices: Lose its protected status, depending on the terms of the local ordinance
Be rebuilt as of right in every case
Be expanded during reconstruction
Be transferred to another parcel in the same district
questions.explanation: Ordinances commonly extinguish the protection when the structure is substantially destroyed or the use is abandoned for a stated period.

questions.prompt: Downzoning refers to:
choices: Rezoning land to a less intensive use or lower density
Lowering the assessed value of property in a district
Reducing the setback requirements in an ordinance
Converting commercial property to residential use by variance
questions.explanation: Downzoning can sharply reduce development value and sometimes prompts regulatory takings claims from affected owners.

questions.prompt: A buffer zone in land use planning is:
choices: A transitional area separating incompatible districts
Land reserved for future municipal buildings
The area between a structure and its lot line
A district in which no development of any kind is permitted
questions.explanation: Buffers ease the transition between, for example, industrial and residential districts, using landscaping, open space, or lower-intensity uses.

questions.prompt: A certificate of occupancy for a newly constructed building is issued after:
choices: Final inspection confirms the work complies with the approved plans and code
The building permit application is approved
The property is conveyed to its first owner
The subdivision plat is filed with the county clerk
questions.explanation: Occupying a structure without a certificate can subject the owner to penalties and typically prevents a lender from funding.

questions.prompt: Deed restrictions and zoning both limit land use. Where the two conflict:
choices: The more restrictive of the two controls
Zoning always supersedes a private restriction
The private restriction always supersedes zoning
The owner may elect which to follow
questions.explanation: They operate independently. A property may be zoned for a use that a recorded covenant forbids, and the covenant still binds the owner.

questions.prompt: Market value is best defined as the price a property should bring in a sale where:
choices: Buyer and seller are typically motivated, well informed, and acting without duress
The seller must sell quickly and accepts the highest available offer
The buyer pays the maximum a lender will finance
The price equals the property's assessed value
questions.explanation: Market value assumes an arm's length transaction with reasonable exposure to the market. A forced sale produces price, not market value.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Valuation Process and Pricing Properties

questions.prompt: The four characteristics that create value in real property are demand, utility, scarcity, and:
choices: Transferability
Location
Durability
Assessment
questions.explanation: Without the legal ability to transfer it, an otherwise desirable property has no market value. The four are often remembered as DUST.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Valuation Process and Pricing Properties

questions.prompt: The principle of conformity holds that a property achieves maximum value when it:
choices: Is reasonably similar to surrounding properties in style, size, and use
Is the largest and most expensive home in the neighborhood
Is the smallest home among larger neighbors
Differs from surrounding properties enough to stand out
questions.explanation: Conformity underlies both regression and progression: an over-improved home is dragged down by its neighbors, and a modest one is lifted by them.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Valuation Process and Pricing Properties

questions.prompt: An owner spends $60,000 on a swimming pool that raises the property's value by $20,000. This illustrates:
choices: The principle of contribution, under which cost does not equal value
The principle of substitution
External obsolescence caused by neighborhood decline
Physical deterioration of a curable kind
questions.explanation: Contribution measures what a component adds to the whole, which is frequently far less than what it cost to install.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Valuation Process and Pricing Properties

questions.prompt: In the cost approach, reproduction cost differs from replacement cost because reproduction cost estimates:
choices: An exact duplicate of the structure using the same materials and design
A structure of equivalent utility using current materials and methods
The depreciated value of the existing improvements
The cost of the land plus the improvements
questions.explanation: Replacement cost is used more often because duplicating obsolete construction is rarely meaningful. Reproduction cost matters for historic properties.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Valuation Process and Pricing Properties

questions.prompt: A home has a badly outdated kitchen that could be economically remodeled. This is:
choices: Curable functional obsolescence
Incurable functional obsolescence
External obsolescence
Physical deterioration
questions.explanation: Obsolescence is curable when the cost to fix it is recovered in added value. A poor floor plan requiring structural change is typically incurable.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Valuation Process and Pricing Properties

questions.prompt: In reconciling the three approaches for a single-family home appraisal, the appraiser typically gives most weight to:
choices: The sales comparison approach
The cost approach
The income capitalization approach
An average of all three approaches
questions.explanation: Reconciliation is a judgment about reliability, not an arithmetic average. Comparable sales best reflect how buyers behave in the residential market.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Valuation Process and Pricing Properties

questions.prompt: A comparable property sold three months ago in a market rising 1% per month. The appraiser should:
choices: Adjust the comparable's sale price upward for market conditions
Adjust the comparable's sale price downward for market conditions
Discard the comparable as too old to use
Adjust the subject property's value downward
questions.explanation: A sale in a rising market understates today's value, so the comparable is adjusted up. Adjustments are always applied to the comparable, never the subject.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Valuation Process and Pricing Properties

questions.prompt: A gross rent multiplier of 120 is derived from a market where a property renting for $2,000 per month sold for:
questions.explanation: GRM based on monthly rent multiplies the rent by the factor: $2,000 x 120 = $240,000. Annual-rent multipliers produce a much smaller factor.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Valuation Process and Pricing Properties

questions.prompt: The principle of anticipation holds that value is created by:
choices: The expectation of future benefits from owning the property
The historical cost of constructing the improvements
The length of time the current owner has held title
The assessed value set by the municipality
questions.explanation: Anticipation is the foundation of the income approach, where value is the present worth of the income stream a buyer expects to receive.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Valuation Process and Pricing Properties

questions.prompt: An appraiser's opinion of value is:
choices: Supported by data and reasoning, but still an opinion rather than a fact
A guarantee of the price the property will bring at sale
Binding on the lender for underwriting purposes
Identical to the property's assessed value
questions.explanation: Two competent appraisers can reach different supported conclusions. This is why a low appraisal is challenged with better data rather than simply disputed.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Valuation Process and Pricing Properties

questions.prompt: In appraising a vacant residential lot, the appraiser will most often rely on:
choices: The sales comparison approach using comparable land sales
The cost approach less accrued depreciation
The income capitalization approach
The gross rent multiplier method
questions.explanation: Land does not depreciate and produces no income by itself, which leaves comparable sales as the meaningful approach.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Valuation Process and Pricing Properties

questions.prompt: A municipality's tax rate is determined by:
choices: Dividing the budget to be raised by the total taxable assessed value in the jurisdiction
The assessor's estimate of average market value
A rate schedule set by the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
The equalization rate applied to the prior year's levy
questions.explanation: This is why a rising assessment does not automatically raise taxes. If total assessed value rises and the budget does not, the rate falls.

questions.prompt: A property assessed at $150,000 in a municipality with a tax rate of 32 mills owes annual taxes of:
questions.explanation: A mill is one-thousandth of a dollar, so 32 mills is $32 per $1,000. ($150,000 / 1,000) x 32 = $4,800.

questions.prompt: A municipality assesses at 40% of market value. A property with a market value of $400,000 carries an assessed value of:
questions.explanation: $400,000 x 0.40 = $160,000. Fractional assessment is why equalization rates are needed to apportion county and school levies fairly.

questions.prompt: Enhanced STAR in New York is available to:
choices: Qualifying senior homeowners meeting an age and income test
All owner-occupied primary residences regardless of age
Veterans with a service-connected disability
Owners of agricultural property in active production
questions.explanation: Basic STAR applies more broadly to primary residences; Enhanced STAR provides a larger exemption to seniors who meet the income limit.

questions.prompt: A property tax exemption available in New York specifically to qualifying former service members is the:
choices: Veterans exemption
STAR exemption
Agricultural assessment
Homestead exemption under the CPLR
questions.explanation: Municipalities elect among several veterans exemption options. The CPLR homestead exemption is creditor protection, not a tax reduction.
questions.citation: NY Real Property Tax Law Article 4

questions.prompt: Unpaid real property taxes in New York may ultimately result in:
choices: A tax foreclosure proceeding that extinguishes the owner's interest
A personal judgment against the owner with no effect on the property
The property being reassessed at a lower value
Referral of the debt to the Department of State
questions.explanation: Because tax liens hold first priority, tax foreclosure wipes out mortgages and most other encumbrances, which is why lenders escrow for taxes.
questions.citation: NY Real Property Tax Law Article 11

questions.prompt: The taxable status date in a New York municipality is significant because it:
choices: Fixes the property's condition and ownership for that year's assessment roll
Sets the deadline for paying the current year's taxes
Marks the date the tax rate is adopted
Establishes when a tax lien may be foreclosed
questions.explanation: Improvements completed after the taxable status date are generally picked up in the following year's roll rather than the current one.

questions.prompt: The tentative assessment roll is published so that:
choices: Owners can review their assessments and file grievances before the roll becomes final
Lenders can calculate escrow requirements for the coming year
Buyers can determine the market value of listed properties
The municipality can set its annual budget
questions.explanation: Grievance Day follows the tentative roll. Once the final roll is filed, administrative challenge for that year is generally foreclosed.
questions.citation: NY Real Property Tax Law Article 5

questions.prompt: An agricultural assessment in New York allows qualifying farmland to be assessed based on:
choices: Its value for agricultural production rather than its development potential
The average assessment of neighboring residential parcels
Fifty percent of its full market value
The price the owner originally paid for the land
questions.explanation: The program eases development pressure on farmland. Converting the land to non-agricultural use triggers payments recapturing prior tax savings.
questions.citation: NY Agriculture and Markets Law Article 25-AA

questions.prompt: A special assessment for a new sidewalk is most commonly apportioned among benefited properties according to:
choices: Front footage along the improvement
Each property's assessed value
The number of occupants in each dwelling
The municipality's equalization rate
questions.explanation: Special assessments track benefit rather than value, and frontage is the usual measure for linear improvements such as sidewalks and sewers.

questions.prompt: A licensee asked by a buyer to predict future property taxes should:
choices: Explain that taxes may change and direct the buyer to the assessor for current figures
Quote the seller's current taxes as the amount the buyer will pay
Estimate based on the purchase price and the current tax rate
Provide a written guarantee of the first year's tax amount
questions.explanation: A sale can trigger reassessment and exemptions belonging to the seller do not transfer, so the seller's current bill can badly understate the buyer's.

questions.prompt: A property owner dissatisfied with the outcome of a board of assessment review grievance may next:
choices: Commence a tax certiorari or small claims assessment review proceeding
Appeal directly to the New York State Department of State
Withhold payment until the assessment is corrected
Request a new assessment from a private appraiser
questions.explanation: Small claims assessment review is the streamlined route available to owner-occupants of residential property; tax certiorari is the broader judicial proceeding.
questions.citation: NY Real Property Tax Law Article 7

questions.prompt: An investor sells a rental property held for six years at a gain. That gain is generally taxed as:
choices: Long-term capital gain, at preferential rates
Ordinary income, at the taxpayer's marginal rate
Tax-free, because the property was held over five years
Passive loss recapture
questions.explanation: Property held more than one year produces long-term capital gain, though depreciation previously taken is recaptured at a different rate.

questions.prompt: Depreciation previously claimed on an investment property is, on sale:
choices: Recaptured and taxed, generally at a higher rate than the long-term capital gain rate
Ignored, because it was already deducted
Added back to the property's adjusted basis
Refunded to the taxpayer as a credit
questions.explanation: Depreciation reduces basis, which increases gain on sale. Recapture is what prevents the deduction from being a permanent tax benefit.

questions.prompt: In a delayed Section 1031 exchange, the taxpayer must identify replacement property within:
choices: 45 days of transferring the relinquished property
180 days of transferring the relinquished property
30 days of transferring the relinquished property
The same tax year as the transfer
questions.explanation: The 45-day identification period runs concurrently with the 180-day period to complete the acquisition. Neither can be extended for convenience.

questions.prompt: A qualified intermediary is used in a Section 1031 exchange to:
choices: Hold the sale proceeds so the taxpayer never has constructive receipt of them
Locate suitable replacement property for the taxpayer
File the exchange documentation with the Internal Revenue Service
Guarantee that the replacement property is of equal value
questions.explanation: Touching the proceeds destroys the deferral. The intermediary exists to prevent constructive receipt between the sale and the purchase.

questions.prompt: A homeowner who has owned and occupied a residence for eighteen months sells at a gain and moves for a new job. The Section 121 exclusion:
choices: May be partially available under the reduced exclusion for a qualifying change in employment
Is entirely unavailable, because the two-year test was not met
Applies in full, because employment relocation waives the test
Applies only if the taxpayer buys a replacement home
questions.explanation: A partial exclusion is available where the sale is due to a change in employment, health, or unforeseen circumstances, prorated by the time actually satisfied.

questions.prompt: Land held as part of an investment property is:
choices: Never depreciable, so the purchase price must be allocated between land and improvements
Depreciated over 27.5 years along with the building
Depreciated over 39 years for residential rental property
Depreciated only if it is improved with paving or landscaping
questions.explanation: Because land is not depreciable, allocating more of the price to improvements increases annual deductions, which makes the allocation a scrutinized figure.

questions.prompt: Rental real estate losses are generally treated under the tax code as:
choices: Passive losses, deductible against passive income subject to limited exceptions
Ordinary business losses fully deductible against any income
Capital losses limited to $3,000 per year
Non-deductible personal expenses
questions.explanation: A limited allowance exists for actively participating owners below certain income levels, and real estate professionals may qualify for different treatment.

questions.prompt: A property acquired by inheritance generally takes a basis equal to:
choices: Its fair market value at the date of the decedent's death
The decedent's original purchase price
The decedent's adjusted basis, carried over unchanged
Zero, until the heir makes capital improvements
questions.explanation: The stepped-up basis eliminates gain accrued during the decedent's ownership. A lifetime gift, by contrast, generally carries over the donor's basis.

questions.prompt: Points paid by a buyer to obtain a mortgage on a principal residence are generally:
choices: Deductible in the year paid, if they meet the requirements for purchase-money points
Never deductible under any circumstances
Added to the property's basis and depreciated
Deductible only when the loan is repaid in full
questions.explanation: Points on a refinance are generally amortized over the loan term instead, which is a common point of confusion for homeowners.

questions.prompt: The federal deduction for state and local taxes, including property taxes, is currently:
choices: Subject to a statutory dollar cap for individual taxpayers
Unlimited for owner-occupied residences
Available only to taxpayers who do not itemize
Limited to taxes paid on investment property
questions.explanation: The SALT cap has particular impact in high-tax states such as New York, where property and income taxes frequently exceed the limit.

questions.prompt: An installment sale allows a seller to:
choices: Report gain proportionately as payments are received across multiple years
Defer the entire gain until the final payment is received
Exclude the gain entirely if payments span more than five years
Convert capital gain into ordinary income at a lower rate
questions.explanation: Spreading gain across years can keep the seller in a lower bracket. Depreciation recapture, however, is generally reported entirely in the year of sale.

questions.prompt: A licensee asked by a client how a sale will affect their income taxes should:
choices: Explain the general concepts and refer the client to a tax professional
Calculate the client's expected tax liability from the sale figures
Advise the client that no tax is due if they reinvest the proceeds
Decline to discuss the transaction's financial aspects at all
questions.explanation: General education is appropriate; specific advice is not. Tax outcomes depend on facts a licensee does not have and is not licensed to evaluate.
questions.citation: DOS 77-hour curriculum § Income Tax Issues in Real Estate Transactions
